title: optimize quant kernels: fused dequant+gemm, smoothquant fusion, and scheduling tweaks
author: Asha Patel
commits: fused dequant+gemm kernel with int8/uint8 path and fp8 fallback
add smoothquant scaling fusion pass into graph loader
scheduler: prefer fused kernels when available and add heuristic for sequence-length-based batching
kv_cache: avoid redundant dequant copies for cached prefixes
microbench: add end-to-end throughput and latency tests for INT8/FP8 paths
docs: perf notes and recommended configs for Dedicated deployments
description: Motivation: quantized inference for common decoder-LLM workloads is currently dominated by dequantization overhead and extra kernels when combining smoothquant scaling with INT8/FP8 model weights. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes to reduce per-token work and improve throughput/latency for quantized models. Changes: 1) fused dequant+GEMM CUDA kernel that accepts INT8/FP8 inputs and applies dequantization and matmul in a single launch, with optional row/column scaling hooks used by smoothquant; 2) smoothquant fusion pass in the model loader that folds scale factors into the fused kernel invocation rather than inserting extra elementwise kernels; 3) scheduler heuristics to prefer fused kernels and adjust batcher windowing for mixed sequence-length workloads to reduce small-batch overheads; 4) KV cache code-path improvements to avoid an extra dequant copy for cached key/value tensors by tracking quantization metadata and reusing fused kernels for cache materialization; 5) microbench harness and perf dashboards updates documenting typical gains. Results: microbench (A100, sequence length 128, beam=1) shows ~1.9x throughput improvement for INT8 end-to-end generation and median p50 latency down by ~28ms compared to previous quant path; FP8 path shows ~1.5x throughput improvement and similar latency wins when smoothquant is active. CI: added unit tests covering fused kernel correctness across quant formats and end-to-end smoke tests. Rollout plan: merged to main behind a runtime feature-flag, enable on Dedicated canaries for a week, collect perf telemetry and enable globally if no regressions. Related: ENG-3421 (quant perf initiative), ENG-3487 (scheduler batching improvements).
